newsitem.title: UK: Four green rates to devalue, stg faces revaluation.
newsitem.headline: Four green rates to devalue, stg faces revaluation.

text.p: Four green currencies will devalue in the European Union's (EU) agrimonetary system on Monday while sterling will enter a 10-day period of assessment for a possible revaluation, the UK's Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) said on Friday.
The four currencies slated for green devaluation are the mark, the guilder, the Austrian schilling and the Belgian franc.

The HGCA calculated the new green rate for the mark as 1.92391 per Ecu from the previous 1.92047, for the Belgian franc as 39.6374 from 39.5483, for the Austrian schilling as 13.5355 from 13.5103 and for the guilder as 2.15840 from 2.15464.
The devaluations followed the continued strength of the Irish punt which will enter its fourth of possibly five 10-day confirmation periods for a future revaluation in the farm grid.
Sterling will only need one confirmation period to be revalued because past devaluations offset any possible revenue losses to farmers as a result of a revaluation.
Green rates are used to calculate EU farm subsidies in national currencies and have no direct impact on foreign exchange markets.
